questions.title: 0/1 Knapsack Max Value
questions.description:
A courier packs a knapsack of capacity W: item i weighs wt[i] and is worth val[i], and each item may be taken at most once. Return the maximum total value that fits without exceeding the capacity — the classic 0/1 knapsack table over (items seen, remaining capacity). Input format: line 1 has n and W; line 2 has n weights; line 3 has n values. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long knapsack_value(const std::vector<long long>& wt, const std::vector<long long>& val, long long W)

Input Format:
Line 1: n and W. Line 2: n weights. Line 3: n values.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= W <= 500, 1 <= wt[i] <= 100, 1 <= val[i] <= 1000

questions.title: ATM Note Split
questions.description:
An ATM pays out using only 500- and 100-rupee notes, giving as many 500s as possible. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void split_notes(int amount, int &fives, int &hundreds)

It must store amount / 500 into fives and (amount % 500) / 100 into hundreds. Amounts are always multiples of 100 — arithmetic only, no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the count of 500-notes, then the count of 100-notes, space-separated.

Constraints:
100 <= amount <= 100000, amount % 100 == 0

questions.title: Anagram Detector
questions.description:
Two lower-case words are anagrams when they contain exactly the same letters with the same multiplicities. Decide with a 26-slot count array (sorting is banned). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool are_anagrams(const std::string &a, const std::string &b)

The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with two lower-case tokens separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line with 1 (anagrams) or 0 (not).

Constraints:
1 <= a.size(), b.size() <= 1000, lower-case letters only

questions.title: Antivirus Sweep Count
questions.description:
An antivirus sweeps a quarantined folder once per minute, removing half of the infected files each sweep (rounded down). Sweep after sweep continues while more than one infected file remains. Return how many sweeps happen for n infected files. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int sweep_count(int n)

It must answer the same question as the loop "while (n > 1) n /= 2;" — how many halvings until n reaches 1.

Input Format:
One line with the infected-file count.

Output Format:
One line with the number of sweeps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Append Task to Print Queue
questions.description:
A print queue appends new jobs at the tail: allocate a Node, walk to the last node and link it there, then return the (unchanged) head. The harness prints the resulting list space-separated. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    Node* append_back(Node* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Attach at Back of Doubly List
questions.description:
Allocate a fresh DNode and link it after the tail: walk to the tail, set tail->next to the node and the node's prev to the tail. Return the (unchanged) head; the harness prints the list forward. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    DNode* dll_push_back(DNode* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting list from head to tail, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Average of Three Doubles
questions.description:
Read and compute with double values. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double average_three(double a, double b, double c)

It must return (a + b + c) / 3. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with three numbers A, B and C.

Output Format:
One line with the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-1000.0 <= A, B, C <= 1000.0

questions.title: Balance Point of the Shelf
questions.description:
A shelf balances at the leftmost index where the total weight strictly to the left equals the total strictly to the right. Return that 0-based index, or -1 when no balance point exists (either side may be empty, summing to 0). Precompute prefix sums and compare each cut point. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int balance_index(const std::vector<long long>& a)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n weights.

Output Format:
One line with the leftmost balance index, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Balanced Code Snippet
questions.description:
A code editor highlights snippets whose brackets do not nest correctly. Brackets come in three kinds: (), [] and {} — and kinds must match LIFO style.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_balanced(const string &s)

It must return true when every bracket in s is closed by the matching kind, false otherwise.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s (single token).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if balanced, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000, s contains only '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}'

questions.title: Best Buy-Then-Sell Timing
questions.description:
A trader reviews a price timeline: pick one day to buy and a LATER day (strictly after) to sell — return the maximum profit prices[j] - prices[i] over all pairs j > i, or -1 when no strictly profitable trade exists. Track the running cheapest price so far (minSoFar) in one pass — sort( is banned. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long max_price_gap(const std::vector<long long>& prices)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n prices.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum profit, or -1 when every trade loses money or breaks even.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 200, 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Best Consecutive Net Gain
questions.description:
A trading desk replays a ledger of daily net gains (negative days possible): return the maximum sum over any NON-EMPTY run of consecutive days — Kadane's algorithm with a running cur sum versus the best seen (sort( is banned). Days can swing to ±10^9, so keep the running totals in long long. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long max_subarray_sum(const std::vector<long long>& a)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n daily net gains.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum non-empty subarray sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, -1000000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Big-O Class Identifier
questions.description:
A teaching tool maps snippet IDs to complexity ranks. The snippets are:
1 → O(n log n), 2 → O(1), 3 → O(n^2), 4 → O(log n), 5 → O(n), 6 → O(2^n).
Rank them from fastest to slowest: O(1) is rank 1, O(log n) rank 2, O(n) rank 3, O(n log n) rank 4, O(n^2) rank 5, O(2^n) rank 6. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int big_o_class(int id)

It must return the rank (1-6) of the snippet with the given id. Use an if-chain — no switch, no containers.

Input Format:
One line with the snippet id (1-6).

Output Format:
One line with the complexity rank.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 6

questions.title: Binary Digits by Recursion
questions.description:
A hardware course displays numbers in base 2. Build the binary representation recursively: the bits of n are the bits of n / 2 followed by the last bit of n. Report the value without leading zeros (n >= 1, so the output always starts with 1). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string to_binary(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the binary representation of n (no leading zeros).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Binary Search on Sorted Data
questions.description:

Output Format:
One line with the index, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, values strictly increasing, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000

questions.title: Bottom-Up Merge Sort
questions.description:
A stack-limited device needs merge sort WITHOUT recursion. Implement it bottom-up: merge runs of width 1, then 2, then 4, ... doubling the width each round until one run covers the array (each round merges consecutive run pairs [i, i+width) and [i+width, i+2*width), clamped to n). Calling a sort routine is banned; no recursion allowed. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> bottom_up_merge(std::vector<int> v)

It must return the vector sorted ascending. The harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Broadcast Reach
questions.description:
A network ops tool floods a firmware broadcast from one device: return how many devices receive it — the size of the set of nodes reachable from start, including start itself. Input format: line 1 has V and E; each of the next E lines has u and v (0-based node ids), one undirected edge per line. The harness builds the adjacency list adj (vector<vector<int>>) with each node's neighbors in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int reachable_count(int V, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj, int start)

Input Format:
Line 1: V and E. Next E lines: u v (undirected edge). Last line: start.

Output Format:
One line with the number of reachable nodes.

Constraints:
2 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Browser Back Button
questions.description:
A browser keeps the visited pages in a stack-like history: the last entry is the current page. Pressing back k times lands on the entry k positions earlier.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string back_state(const vector<string> &history, int k)

It must return the page shown after pressing back k times: history[history.size() - 1 - k].

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the number of history entries.
Line 2: n page names (single tokens).
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting page name.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k < n

questions.title: Browser Tabs Deque Move
questions.description:
A tab manager is a deque: the user can yank any open tab and push it to the front without disturbing the order of the others.

The id appears exactly once in tabs; it must end up first, with all other tabs keeping their relative order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n tab ids.
Line 3: id — the tab to move (appears exactly once).

Output Format:
One line with the new tab order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000000 <= ids <= 1000000

questions.title: Build Order Cycle Alert
questions.description:
A CI system refuses builds whose dependency graph contains a directed cycle: return 1 when a cycle exists, else 0. Detect it with DFS colors (state: 0 = unvisited, 1 = on the recursion stack, 2 = finished) — queue< is banned, the reference recurses. Input format: line 1 has V and E; each of the next E lines has u and v (0-based node ids), one directed edge u -> v per line. The harness builds the adjacency list adj (vector<vector<int>>) with each node's out-neighbors in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(int V, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj)

Input Format:
Line 1: V and E. Next E lines: u v (directed edge u -> v).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the directed graph has a cycle, else 0.

Constraints:
2 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Build the Min-Heap In Place
questions.description:
A scheduler converts an arbitrary priorities array into a valid min-heap IN PLACE with Floyd's method: call sift-down on every node from index n/2 - 1 down to 0 (a node sinks while a smaller child exists). The harness prints the repaired array space-separated. std::sort, make_heap and priority_queue are banned — write the sift-down yourself with while loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void build_min_heap(std::vector<int>& heap)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the array after Floyd's build, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Can the Morning Routine Be Scheduled?

Input format: line 1 has V and E; each of the next E lines has u and v (0-based node ids), one directed edge u -> v per line.     int is_schedulable(int V, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj)

Line 1: V and E. Next E lines: u v (directed edge u -> v).

2 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

    int ring_length(DNode* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (ring order).

1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

Input Format:
One line with two tokens separated by a space.

Output Format:

1 <= a.size(), b.size() <= 1000, letters and digits

questions.title: Children Sum Property Check

The harness builds the tree from line 1: n and line 2: n level-order values (-1 = missing node). The program scaffolding (includes, the TNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int children_sum_ok(TNode* root)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n level-order values (-1 = NULL).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if every non-leaf node equals the sum of its children, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= values <= 100000

questions.title: Circular Queue Enqueue Code

A brute-force triple checker runs "for i in 1..n, for j in i+1..n, for k in j+1..n" — its body executes once per combination of three distinct indices, i.e. C(n, 3) = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6 times. Return that count with a closed-form formula — no loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long triple_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the triple count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

Solve iteratively in O(1) extra memory — sets, maps, hash containers and vectors are banned. Report 1 if a cycle exists, else 0. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(Node* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: pos (-1 = no link, else 0-based index < n).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the list contains a cycle, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1 <= pos < n

One line with the ordered words.

1 <= n <= 200, 1 <= word length <= 20, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Workbook After k Insertion Steps
questions.description:
A workbook's page counts are being sorted by insertion sort. Predict the state after EXACTLY k steps, where step i (i = 1, 2, 3, ...) fully inserts the element at index i into the sorted prefix v[0..i-1]. k may exceed n-1 — the workbook is then fully sorted. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> insertion_after_k(std::vector<int> v, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the workbook after exactly k insertion steps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k <= 1000

questions.title: Zone Labels for Every District
questions.description:
A census labels every district with its zone id: fill out with V entries — out[i] = the id of the connected component containing i, numbering components 0, 1, 2, ... by their smallest member. Recurse over the adjacency lists — queue< is banned. The harness prints out space-separated. Input format: line 1 has V and E; each of the next E lines has u and v (0-based node ids), one undirected edge per line. The harness builds the adjacency list adj (vector<vector<int>>) with each node's neighbors in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void component_labels(int V, const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& adj, std::vector<int>& out)

Input Format:
Line 1: V and E. Next E lines: u v (undirected edge).

Output Format:
One line with V component ids, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V
